{{Short description|Russian mathematician (1905–1980)}}
{{expand Russian|topic=bio|date=January 2022}}
{{use dmy dates|date=January 2022|cs1-dates=y}}

'''Dmitrii Abramovich Raikov''' ({{langx|ru|Дмитрий Абрамович Райков}}<!-- Raikow, Dmitri Abramowitsch -->, born 11 November 1905 in Odessa; died 1980 in Moscow) was a Russian mathematician who studied [[functional analysis]].

Raikov studied in Odessa and Moscow, graduating in 1929. He was secretary of the [[Komsomol]] at Moscow State University and was active in the 1929–1930 campaign against the mathematician [[Dmitri Fyodorovich Egorov]]. At that time he and his fellow campaigners also rejected non-applied research, but this soon changed. In 1933, he was dismissed from the Communist Party on charges of Trotskyism and exiled to [[Voronezh]], but was rehabilitated two years later and returned to Moscow. From 1938 to 1948, he was at the Mathematical Institute of the [[USSR Academy of Sciences|Academy of Sciences]] and in the [[Second World War]] in the militia. He was habilitated (Russian doctorate) in 1941 with [[Aleksandr Yakovlevich Khinchin]] at the [[Lomonosov University]]<ref name="MGP"/> and in 1950 became professor. He taught at the Pedagogical Institute in [[Kostroma]] and from 1952 in Shuysky, before he taught from 1957 at the State Pedagogical University in Moscow. He also supervised students and taught at Lomonosov University.

[[Israel Gelfand]] and Raikov's 1943 theorem<ref name="Gelfand-Raikov_1943"/> states that a [[locally compact group]] <math>G</math> is completely determined by its (possibly infinite-dimensional) [[irreducible representation|irreducible]] [[Group algebra of a locally compact group|unitary representation]]s: for every two elements <math>g,h</math> of <math>G</math> there is an irreducible unitary representation <math>\rho</math> with <math>\rho (g) \neq \rho (h)</math>.<ref name="NCAT"/>

He also worked on [[probability theory]], for example in 1938 he proved an equivalent of the [[Cramér's decomposition theorem|Cramér's theorem]] for the [[Poisson distribution]].

He edited the Russian editions of [[Nicolas Bourbaki]]'s "Topology and Integration Theory" and translated numerous other mathematical works from Italian, English and German, for example the lectures on the theory of [[algebraic number]]s by [[Erich Hecke]], the book ''[[Moderne Algebra]]'' by [[Bartel Leendert van der Waerden]], the <!-- Aufgaben und Lehrsätze aus der Analysis -->''[[Problems and Theorems in Analysis]]'' by [[George Pólya]] and [[Gábor Szegő]], the <!-- Einführung in die Theorie der Fourier-Integrale -->introduction to the theory of [[Fourier integral]]s by [[Edward Charles Titchmarsh]], the <!-- Vorlesungen über partielle Differentialgleichungen -->lectures on [[partial differential equation]]s by [[Francesco Tricomi]], the <!-- Einführung in die Differential- und Integralrechnung -->introduction to [[differential calculus|differential]] and [[integral calculus]] by [[Edmund Landau]], the <!-- Monographie über divergenten Reihen -->monograph on [[series (mathematics)|divergent series]] by [[Godfrey Harold Hardy]] and the [[vector space|finite dimensional vector spaces]] by [[Paul Halmos]].

==Works==
* with [[Israel Moiseevich Gelfand]], [[Georgi Evgen'evich Shilov]]: Kommutative normierte Algebren (Commutative normalized algebras). Berlin, [[Deutscher Verlag der Wissenschaften]], 1964 (first Russian, 1960).
* with Gelfand: <!-- Kommutative normierte Ringe -->Commutative normalized rings (Russian). Uspekhi Mat. [[Nauka (publisher)|Nauka]], 1946
* Vector spaces. Groningen, Netherlands: [[P. Noordhoff]], 1965 (first in Russian, 1962).
* with <!-- Mikhail Shamshonovich Tsalenko --> Michail Šamšonovič Calenko [Михаил Шамшонович Цаленко], Vladimir Borisovich Gisin [Владимир Борисович Гисин]: <!-- Категория с инволюцией --> Ordered categories with involution. Warsaw, Mathematical Institute of the Academy of Sciences. 1984. [http://pldml.icm.edu.pl/pldml/element/bwmeta1.element.zamlynska-e0af96c4-aca3-4890-a28f-605f9b788bad/c/rm22701.pdf<!-- https://web.archive.org/web/20201126035011/http://pldml.icm.edu.pl/pldml/element/bwmeta1.element.zamlynska-e0af96c4-aca3-4890-a28f-605f9b788bad/c/rm22701.pdf -->]
* <!-- Eindimensionale mathematische Analysis -->One-dimensional mathematical analysis (Russian). Moscow, 1982.
* with E. Gusatinskaia: Analyse mathématique multidimensionnelle<!-- Analysis mathématique multidimensionalnelle -->. Moscow: [[MIR Moscow|MIR]], 1993 (first as <!-- Mehrdimensionale mathematische Analysis -->''Multidimensional Mathematical Analysis'' (Russian). Moscow, 1989).
* with [[Ilya Nikolaevich Bronshtein]]: Справочник по елементарнои математике, механике и физике (Russian) [Handbook of elementary mathematics, mechanics and physics]. Moscow, 1943.<ref name="Bronshtein-Raikov_1943"/>
* with [[Boris Nikolayevich Delaunay]]: <!-- Analytische Geometrie -->Analytical Geometry (Russian). 2 volumes, Moscow, 1948, 1949.
